problem.source: Oh, Scrimshaw - Identities from representation theory, arXiv:1805.00113v1, Appendix A, Conjecture A.4
problem.statement: For M_0=1, M_{n+1}=M_n+sum_{r<n} q^{r+1} M_r M_{n-1-r}: det[M_{i+j+2k}(q)]_{i,j=0}^{n-1} in Z_{>=0}[q] for all k,n >= 1, coefficientwise; or a genuine counterexample.
problem.first_batch_relation: sibling record 339076 (typo refutation) does not exclude this problem

model_provider: GLM (glm-5.3-flash-thinking-high), pi coding agent, solo lane, no subagents

outcome.proved: k=1 (shift 2) case: explicit monomial formula for Delta_n^{(2)}, all coefficients +1
outcome.counterexample: none found; even shifts verified positive for k<=4 through n=7 (k=1: proved, n<=14)

verification.method: exact dict-of-monomial polynomial arithmetic; fraction-free Bareiss determinants; no floating point
checks: Delta_n^{(2)} closed form == direct Hankel determinant for n <= 14
Claim R: Delta_n^{(r)} = q^{beta_n} det[(B^r) block] for r <= 7, n <= 5
square identity det[(B^{2k})_n] = q^{C(n,2)} sum_M det[T_{[0,n),M}]^2 q^{sum M} for k = 1..3, n <= 5
positivity scan: k = 1..4, n <= 7 all positive-coefficient
odd shifts r = 3,5: negative coefficients at n = 3,4 (matches source)
